outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
treatment with continuous positive airway pressure
cohort: The cohort included healthy women with uncomplicated pregnancies and no medical interventions during delivery in Denmark between 2003 and 2013, encompassing 6,395 home births and 266,604 hospital births.
finding: This study indicates that home births in Denmark are characterized by a high level of safety owing to low rates of perinatal mortality and morbidity.
mod_finding: Infants born at home had significantly lower frequencies of admission to a neonatal intensive care unit and treatment with continuous positive airway pressure compared to hospital births, though a slightly, but significantly increased rate of early neonatal death was found among infants delivered by nulliparous women at home.
